docs.title: Zuhura: Mars Digital Twin & Scientific Intelligence
docs.text: Welcome to the technical knowledge base for Zuhura, an interactive 3D digital representation of Mars and planetary research intelligence platform designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

docs.title: Mission & Vision
docs.text: Unlike conventional web maps, Zuhura models the physical reality of planetary exploration: - Mars-Specific Geodesy: Strict IAU/IAG 2015 WGCCRE ellipsoidal references and Areoid elevation datums. - Traceable Scientific Data: Deep integration with NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) and USGS Astrogeology. - Grounded AI Intelligence: A domain-specific research assistant grounded in indexed observation footprints, peer-reviewed literature, and validated spatial tools.

docs.title: Platform Modules
docs.text:
1. Planetary Visualization Engine (zuhura-frontend): Built on CesiumJS, customized with Martian atmospheric scattering and Quantized Mesh terrain streaming.
  2. Backend & Spatial Services (zuhura-backend): Asynchronous FastAPI service orchestrating spatial queries, coordinate conversions, and AI pipelines.
  3. Contracts & Specifications (zuhura-api): OpenAPI 3.1 definitions, JSON schemas, and STAC extensions.
  4. Data Pipelines (zuhura-data): Automated PDS harvesters, COG pyramid converters, and coordinate validators.

docs.title: AI Scientific Intelligence Methodology
docs.text: The Ask Zuhura assistant is an evidence-grounded scientific intelligence system designed specifically for planetary researchers, educators, and mission planners.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
1. Zero Raw SQL Execution: The assistant interacts with databases exclusively through strictly validated, parameterized Pydantic tool schemas.
  2. Context-Aware Spatial Ingestion: The system continuously ingests camera position (lat, lon, altitude) and active layer IDs from the Cesium globe.
  3. Mandatory Citations & Provenance: Every scientific claim must be supported by an indexed dataset ID or peer-reviewed DOI.
  4. Transparent Data Gaps: The assistant explicitly acknowledges observation limits (e.g. indicating when a location only has 100 m/px THEMIS data rather than 25 cm/px HiRISE coverage).

docs.title: Controlled Spatial Tools
docs.text:
• get_elevation_at_point(lat, lon): Samples surface elevation relative to MOLA Areoid.
  • get_elevation_profile(start_point, end_point, samples): Calculates transect cross-sections.
  • search_features(bbox, min_diameter_km): Retrieves verified IAU craters and formations.
  • query_dataset_catalog(bbox, category): Lists available observation footprints.
  • search_mission_traverses(lat, lon): Locates nearby surface landers or rover traverses.

docs.title: Zuhura System Architecture
docs.text: Zuhura is structured as a Modular Monolith for Application Services paired with High-Performance Asynchronous Data Engines.

docs.title: Architecture Components
docs.text:
1. Planetary Rendering Engine (zuhura-frontend):
  2. WebGL2 CesiumJS client customized with the IAU 2015 Mars Biaxial Ellipsoid.
  3. Level-of-Detail (LOD) progressive terrain and imagery streaming via Quantized Mesh and Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) HTTP range requests.

  4. Zustand-driven global state synchronizing camera telemetry, active layers, and feature inspections.

  5. Backend & AI Orchestrator (zuhura-backend):

  6. Python FastAPI modular monolith.
  7. Geodesy transformation engine converting between planetographic and planetocentric coordinates.

  8. Grounded AI assistant utilizing map viewport context, parameterized spatial tools, and strict provenance tracking.

  9. Storage & Database Tier:

  10. PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS 3.4: High-performance spatial indexing of planetary features, craters, and observation footprints.
  11. pgvector: Dense vector similarity search for scientific literature and PDS dataset metadata.
  12. MinIO / S3: Object storage serving COGs and Quantized Mesh terrain tiles.
  13. Redis 7.2: Caching for tile responses and distributed task broker.

docs.title: Scientific Data Catalog Guide
docs.text: Zuhura indexes authoritative planetary datasets from NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) nodes, the PDS Orbital Data Explorer (ODE), USGS Astrogeology Science Center, and ESA Planetary Science Archive (PSA).

docs.title: Canonical Data Processing Tiers
docs.text:
To ensure scientific honesty and prevent simulations or models from being confused with direct orbital telemetry, every dataset in Zuhura is cataloged under a strict derivation tier:

  1. Level 1 (Raw Observation): Uncalibrated instrument telemetry (e.g. raw PDS EDRs).
  2. Level 2 (Calibrated): Radiometrically calibrated data products (e.g. MRO CRISM radiance spectra, HiRISE RDR).
  3. Level 3 (Derived Product): Georeferenced, map-projected orthomosaics and digital elevation models (e.g. MOLA MEGDR, Viking MDIM 2.1, Jezero HiRISE mosaic).
  4. Level 4 (Interpretation): Peer-reviewed geological maps, fault trace databases, and stratigraphical classifications (e.g. USGS SIM 3292).
  5. Level 5 (Simulation): Planetary atmospheric general circulation models (GCMs) and hypothetical thermal/climate simulations.

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text:
• Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG): Standard for gridded rasters. Enables HTTP range requests from browser clients.
  • Quantized Mesh 1.0: Hierarchical 3D terrain streaming format used by CesiumJS for Mars topography.
  • GeoParquet: Columnar spatial storage for planetary feature catalogs (craters, landing sites).
  • STAC 1.0.0: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog metadata specification with the Zuhura Mars Extension.

docs.title: Developer Quickstart Guide
docs.text: This guide describes how to run and test the complete Zuhura Mars Digital Twin locally.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker & Docker Compose (v2.20+)
  • Python 3.12+
  • Node.js 20+
  • PROJ 9+ (for local geospatial coordinate development)

docs.title: 1. Local Environment Setup
docs.text:
# Clone or navigate to the Zuhura organization directory
cd /path/to/Zuhura

# Run the automated development setup script
./zuhura/scripts/dev-setup.sh

docs.title: 2. Launching Supporting Services (PostgreSQL + PostGIS, Redis, MinIO)
docs.text:
cd zuhura/docker
docker compose up -d postgres redis minio minio-init

Verify connectivity:

../scripts/healthcheck.sh

docs.title: 3. Running the Backend Service
docs.text:
cd zuhura-backend
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
uvicorn zuhura.api.main:app --reload --port 8000

API Documentation will be accessible at: http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: 4. Running the Frontend Application
docs.text:
cd zuhura-frontend
npm install
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:3000 to interact with the Mars globe.

docs.title: 5. Running the Test Suite
docs.text:
# Backend Geodesy & API integration tests
cd zuhura-backend
pytest -v

# Frontend Geodesy unit tests
cd zuhura-frontend
npm run test:run

docs.title: 2.1 Multi-Objective Cost Model
docs.text:
Traverses are evaluated using an A* pathfinding algorithm over the MOLA DEM grid. Edge weights account for: $$\text{Cost} = \Delta s \times \left(1 + k_{\text{slope}} \cdot \left(\frac{\theta}{\theta_{\text{ref}}}\right)^2\right) \times \left(1 + k_{\text{roughness}} \cdot \frac{\text{TRI}}{\text{TRI}_{\text{ref}}}\right)$$

If local slope $\theta > \theta_{\text{max}}$, the segment is marked as an impassable obstacle or high-risk hazard.

  • Crew Traverser: Max climbable slope 14°, critical slope 20°, step obstacle 0.30 m.
  • Scout Hexacopter: Max climbable slope 45°, critical slope 60°, obstacle 5.0 m.

docs.title: Mars Coordinate Reference Systems & Geodesy
docs.text: Planetary bodies do not follow Earth terrestrial conventions. Earth GIS tools assume a WGS84 ellipsoid ($a = 6378137\text{ m}$) with mean sea level datums. Mars requires explicit celestial geodetic formulations.

docs.title: 1. Reference Ellipsoid (IAU/IAG 2015 WGCCRE)
docs.text:
Zuhura adopts the official IAU/IAG Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements (2015) standard:

Parameter Value Definition Semi-Major Equatorial Axis ($A$) $3,396,190.0\text{ m}$ Equatorial radius Semi-Minor Polar Axis ($C$) $3,376,200.0\text{ m}$ Polar radius Flattening ($f$) $\approx 0.005886$ $f = (A - C) / A$ Inverse Flattening ($1/f$) $\approx 169.81$ Reciprocal flattening Volumetric Mean Radius $3,389,500.0\text{ m}$ Spherical approximation

docs.title: 2. Planetocentric vs Planetographic Latitude
docs.text:
• Planetocentric Latitude ($\phi_c$): Angle between the equatorial plane and a line drawn from the center of the planet. Used by modern IAU standards, MRO instruments, and Zuhura.
  • Planetographic Latitude ($\phi_g$): Angle between the equatorial plane and the normal vector to the reference surface. Used in historical Viking and Mariner maps.

$$\tan(\phi_c) = \left( \frac{C}{A} \right)^2 \tan(\phi_g) = (1 - f)^2 \tan(\phi_g)$$

At mid-latitudes ($45^\circ$), confusing these two conventions results in a $\sim 20.4\text{ km}$ spatial offset on the Martian surface! Zuhura mathematically converts all legacy products during ingestion.

docs.title: 3. Longitude Convention: East-Positive
docs.text:
Modern cartography mandates Planetocentric East-positive longitude ($0^\circ \text{ to } 360^\circ$), centered at the Airy-0 crater in Sinus Meridiani ($0.0^\circ$ longitude). Historical West-positive coordinates are normalized using:

$$\lambda_{\text{east}} = (360^\circ - \lambda_{\text{west}}) \pmod{360^\circ}$$

docs.title: 4. Topography Reference Datum: Mars Areoid
docs.text: Mars has no oceans. Elevation ($z = 0$) is defined relative to the Mars Areoid (MOLA GMM-2B gravitational equipotential surface) calculated from Mars Global Surveyor Doppler tracking and laser altimeter observations.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Mission Statement
docs.text:
The Zuhura Mars Digital Twin has completed Stages 1 through 8, establishing an authoritative scientific data catalog, validated MOLA elevation baselines ($463\text{ m/px}$), Quantized-Mesh 1.0 terrain streaming, and rigorous geodesic terrain intelligence.

However, when exploring the Mars globe, users experience noticeable visual limitations: 1. From planetary orbit, Mars displays an artificial, pseudo-colored elevation colormap rather than the authentic ochre, tan, and dark basaltic hues of the real planet. 2. When zooming into regional and local surfaces, imagery becomes blurry and pixelated because tiles are clamped at zoom level 7 ($z \le 7$). 3. Authoritative high-resolution datasets on disk (the 12.74 GB USGS Viking MDIM 2.1 global color mosaic at $231.54\text{ m/px}$, CTX at $5.55\text{ m/px}$, and HiRISE at $0.25\text{ m/px}$) are either not served through the tile engine or rendered merely as vector polygon outlines. 4. Navigation controls lack the fluid, momentum-based continuous zoom, zoom-to-cursor, tilt/orbit mechanics, and location search characteristic of Google Earth.

This document presents the Phase A Technical Audit and details the engineering plan to elevate Zuhura into a visually stunning, photorealistic, and fluid Mars exploration twin grounded entirely in scientifically validated mission datasets.

docs.title: 2. Phase A Audit: Root Cause Analysis
2.1 Why Does Mars Currently Look Blurry or Artificial?
docs.text:
A comprehensive audit of the backend tile pipelines and CesiumJS frontend uncovered five primary root causes:

[CURRENT ARCHITECTURE BOTTLENECK]
Raw 12.74 GB Viking Mosaic (Striped, No Overviews) ---> NOT TILED / NOT SERVED
MOLA Elevation COG (463 m/px) ---> Dynamic GDAL Warp ---> Pseudo-Color Ramp ("terrain")
                                                                    │
                                                                    ▼
Cesium UrlTemplateImageryProvider (CLAMPS AT LEVEL 7) <─────────────┘
                                    │
                                    ▼  (Zooming closer than Level 7)
               Cesium stretches Level 7 pixels by 4x - 32x
               ===> SEVERE BLURRINESS & PIXELATION <===
  1. Base Texture Is an Elevation Colormap, Not Natural Martian Albedo:
  2. In MarsGlobe.tsx, the active base imagery provider points to: /api/v1/tiles/cog/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?colormap=terrain
  3. This endpoint takes the single-band MOLA elevation raster and applies a matplotlib rainbow/terrain colormap (blues, greens, browns, snow-white peaks). While useful for topographic inspection, it looks artificial, saturated, and un-photographic from orbit.
  4. Hard Clamp at Zoom Level 7 ($z \le 7$):
  5. The Cesium imagery provider configuration sets minimumLevel: 0, maximumLevel: 7.
  6. In Cesium's GeographicTilingScheme, Level 7 consists of only $128 \times 64$ tiles globally ($\approx 83.3\text{ km}$ per tile, corresponding to $\approx 325\text{ m/px}$ at the equator).
  7. When users zoom into regional or local surface views (levels 8 to 14), Cesium ceases requesting higher-resolution tiles and merely stretches level 7 texture pixels, creating extreme blurriness.
  8. The 12.74 GB Viking MDIM 2.1 Global Color Mosaic Is Un-Tiled on Disk:
  9. The authoritative USGS Astrogeology Viking MDIM 2.1 global color mosaic (Mars_Viking_MDIM21_ClrMosaic_global_232m.tiff) is located in zuhura-data/data/raw/viking/mdim21/.
  10. Dimensions: $92,160 \times 46,080$ pixels, 3 Bands (RGB Byte), native posting $231.54\text{ m/px}$ ($2\times$ sharper than MOLA).
  11. Performance Diagnostic: The file is currently striped ($92,160 \times 1$) with zero internal tile partitioning and zero overviews. A single $512\times 512$ tile read from this raw file takes $2,352\text{ ms}$ because GDAL must seek and scan through gigabytes of raw scanlines. It cannot be served directly on-the-fly without conversion into an optimized Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG).
  12. CTX and HiRISE Layers Are Rendered as Vector Polygons, Not Draped Raster Tiles:
  13. In MarsGlobe.tsx, CTX ($5.55\text{ m/px}$) is currently rendered as a translucent gold rectangle polygon (Cesium.Color.GOLD.withAlpha(0.25)). The actual 35 MB surface image is never decoded or rendered.
  14. HiRISE ($0.25\text{ m/px}$) is rendered as a single static image rectangle over Jezero without multi-resolution LOD mipmapping or progressive resolution streaming.
  15. Frontend Cesium Camera & Rendering Defaults:
  16. globe.maximumScreenSpaceError is set to the default of 2.0, producing coarser terrain meshes than the GPU can easily render.
  17. globe.tileCacheSize is set to the default of 100, which evicts tiles prematurely during zoom operations and creates noticeable tile refetch stuttering.
  18. Atmospheric horizon scattering and limb haze are unconfigured.

docs.title: 1. Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) Generation for Viking MDIM 2.1:
docs.text:
• We will convert the un-overviewed 12.74 GB striped TIFF into a high-performance Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (viking_mdim21_global_cog.tif) using GDAL with 8-thread parallelism: bash gdal_translate zuhura-data/data/raw/viking/mdim21/Mars_Viking_MDIM21_ClrMosaic_global_232m.tiff \ zuhura-data/data/processed/viking/viking_mdim21_global_cog.tif \ -of COG -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co QUALITY=85 -co OVERVIEWS=ALL \ -co RESAMPLING=AVERAGE -co NUM_THREADS=ALL_CPUS
  • Estimated Output Size: $\approx 1.8\text{ GB}$ (fitting easily in the $736\text{ GB}$ available disk space).
  • Performance Impact: Reading any $256\times 256$ tile from the COG drops from $2,352\text{ ms}$ to $< 8\text{ ms}$ ($300\times$ speedup).

docs.title: 2. Upgraded High-Throughput Imagery Tile Endpoint (/api/v1/tiles/viking/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg):
docs.text:
• Implement direct window reads into COG overviews without slow in-memory gdal.Warp re-projections.
  • Support levels $z=0$ through $z=9$ (native $231\text{ m/px}$ resolution).
  • Add disk caching in data/tiles/cache/viking/ with HTTP Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 and ETag validation.

docs.title: 3. Georeferenced Regional CTX & Local HiRISE Tile Streaming:
docs.text:
• Georeference CTX P02_001820_1984_XI_18N282W into a GeoTIFF using the 4 corner ground control points from the official PDS ODE catalog ($77.04^\circ\text{E}$ to $77.62^\circ\text{E}$, $17.88^\circ\text{N}$ to $18.65^\circ\text{N}$).
  • Georeference HiRISE PSP_004299_1985_MRGB using the official PDS ODE KML boundary ($77.5158^\circ\text{E}$ to $77.6537^\circ\text{E}$, $18.2876^\circ\text{N}$ to $18.5834^\circ\text{N}$).
  • Serve CTX and HiRISE tiles via /api/v1/tiles/ctx/{z}/{x}/{y}.png and /api/v1/tiles/hirise/{z}/{x}/{y}.png for seamless progressive resolution draping.

docs.title: 2. Photorealistic Martian Lighting & Atmosphere:
docs.text:
• Atmospheric Horizon Scattering: Fine-tune skyAtmosphere Rayleigh/Mie scattering parameters with Martian dust extinction ($\lambda_{\text{red}} = 650\text{ nm}, \lambda_{\text{green}} = 570\text{ nm}, \lambda_{\text{blue}} = 470\text{ nm}$).

  • Visual Depth Tuning:
  • maximumScreenSpaceError: 1.25 (improved mesh geometric fidelity).
  • tileCacheSize: 1000 (eliminates tile refetch stutter during rapid zoom).
  • Texture filtering set to LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR for distortion-free oblique view angles.

docs.title: 2. Navigation Interaction Mechanics:
docs.text:
• Inertial Mouse-Wheel Zoom-to-Cursor: Camera zooms towards the 3D surface point directly beneath the mouse cursor, allowing users to dive straight into a target crater without centering first.
  • Double-Click Fly-To: Double-clicking any Martian terrain point initiates a smooth, banked parabolic camera transition to that location.
  • Continuous Tilt and Orbit: Intuitive right-click and middle-click drag to smoothly tilt the horizon and orbit around any geological structure.
  • Ground Clearance Protection: Automatic camera elevation clamping (minimumCollisionTerrainHeight: 50.0) prevents the camera from penetrating below the 3D terrain mesh.

docs.text:

  • Rover Touchdown Sites: Perseverance, Curiosity, Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, Viking 1, Viking 2, Zhurong.
  • Direct Coordinate Entry: e.g. 18.38N, 77.58E.

  • True Camera Altitude above Areoid.
  • Active Imagery Source & Resolution (Viking MDIM 2.1: 232 m/px $\rightarrow$ CTX: 5.55 m/px $\rightarrow$ HiRISE: 0.25 m/px).

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Audit Mandate
docs.text:
The Zuhura Mars Digital Twin and Scientific Intelligence Platform represents a federated, multi-tier planetary information system designed to support interactive geospatial visualization, deterministic scientific calculation, and AI-assisted planetary exploration.

This audit assesses the structural integrity, component coupling, API contracts, deployment configurations, and automated test coverage across all seven repositories in the GitHub organization https://github.com/Zuhura-Mars: 1. zuhura-backend (FastAPI, GDAL, PyProj, GeoTIFF/NetCDF raster engines, AI Scientist tool registry, InSight interior models, A* routing) 2. zuhura-frontend (React 18, CesiumJS, Three.js WebGL, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, Vite) 3. zuhura-data (Planetary Data System [PDS] ingestion pipelines, STAC catalog builders, MOLA correction, quantized-mesh terrain generation) 4. zuhura-api (OpenAPI 3.1 specifications, JSON schemas, Mars STAC extensions) 5. zuhura-docs (MkDocs Material technical documentation, scientific methodology specifications, architecture reports) 6. zuhura (Root orchestration, Docker Compose environment, init-db SQL, system operational scripts) 7. .github (Organization profile, unified GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows, issue templates)

The audit was executed under the strict directive: $$\text{PRESERVE} \longrightarrow \text{AUDIT} \longrightarrow \text{VALIDATE} \longrightarrow \text{IMPROVE} \longrightarrow \text{EXTEND} \longrightarrow \text{INTEGRATE} \longrightarrow \text{TEST} \longrightarrow \text{DOCUMENT} \longrightarrow \text{DEPLOY}$$

docs.title: 3.1 Repository: zuhura-backend
docs.text:
• Primary Role: Scientific computation, spatial queries, terrain analysis, routing, visual localization, AI research orchestration.
  • Tech Stack: Python 3.12+, FastAPI, GDAL 3.8+, PyProj, NumPy, SciPy, Pydantic v2, Uvicorn.
  • Key Modules:
  • zuhura.geodesy: Implements IAU/IAG 2015 WGCCRE biaxial ellipsoid geodesy ($A = 3,396,190\text{ m}$, $C = 3,376,200\text{ m}$, $1/f = 169.81$). Rigorous coordinate transformations between planetocentric latitude/east-longitude and MCMF Cartesian coordinates.
  • zuhura.terrain_intelligence: Horn (1981) 8-neighbor quadratic surface fitting for metric slope gradients, aspect, and Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI).
  • zuhura.interior.model: InSight SEIS geophysical model synthesizing crustal layers, mantle, basal molten silicate layer, and liquid core.
  • zuhura.navigation.router: A* cost-distance traverser over MOLA/DEM grids with vehicle mobility limits (Perseverance, Curiosity, Dune Buggy, Aerial Scout).
  • zuhura.pinpoint.engine: Morphological feature extraction and ground-truth landscape matching.
  • zuhura.ai.tools: 14 deterministic scientific tools exposed to the Mars AI Scientist.
  • Strengths: Strict Pydantic input schemas; mathematically sound geodetic projections; sub-millisecond LRU spatial caching; zero mock fallbacks for core geodesy.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • Scientific Provenance: Lack of uniform epistemic classification tags (OBSERVED, MEASURED, DERIVED, MODEL_ESTIMATED, SIMULATED, PROVISIONAL, UNVERIFIED) on all endpoint outputs.
  • Mobility Model Simplification: Slope penalty currently models mechanical slip using simple trigonometric scaling without explicit wheel soil-mechanics (Bekker theory) or solar insolation dynamic cost.
  • Interior Model Plurality: The single default profile masks the published variance between the 2021 large-core model ($R=1,830\text{ km}$) and the 2023 basal molten silicate layer model ($R=1,650\text{ km}$).
  • Observability: Lacks OpenTelemetry tracing and Prometheus metrics endpoints.

docs.title: 3.2 Repository: zuhura-frontend
docs.text:
• Primary Role: User interface, 3D planetary digital twin, interactive geospatial analysis, real-time telemetry display.
  • Tech Stack: React 18, TypeScript 5, Vite, CesiumJS 1.119+, Three.js r128+, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React.
  • Key Components:
  • MarsGlobe.tsx: Cesium viewer configured with custom IAU 2015 Mars ellipsoid, Viking MDIM 2.1, MRO CTX, and MRO HiRISE tile layers. High-DPI canvas scaling (devicePixelRatio), MSAA anti-aliasing, and disabled ground atmospheric wash.
  • XRayMars3DModal.tsx: Interactive Three.js WebGL 3D model with OrbitControls, dynamic cutaway angle slider ($0^\circ-180^\circ$), exploded shell slider, interactive 3D raycast layer picking, and animated seismic wave paths.
  • PinpointRouteHUD.tsx: Interactive click-to-route HUD managing departure and arrival pins, distance, climb, travel sols, and GeoJSON export.
  • HoverIntelligenceTooltip.tsx: Real-time hover HUD with 0ms dynamic description switching across 78 IAU features and 18 regional provinces.
  • Strengths: High performance 60 fps rendering; decoupled state management in Zustand; crisp high-DPI surface presentation.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • Single Imagery Provider Fallback: Local mock raster server must gracefully fallback to public NASA/USGS WMTS tiles when local tile servers are offline.
  • Measurement Tools: Missing dedicated interactive geodesic distance ruler and polygon area calculation tools on the globe.
  • Session History: Lacks client-side persistence for researcher bookmarks, annotations, and route history across page reloads.

docs.title: 3.3 Repository: zuhura-data
docs.text:
• Primary Role: Ingestion, validation, correction, and tiling of planetary datasets.
  • Tech Stack: Python 3.12+, GDAL, Rasterio, NumPy, NetCDF4, PyYAML, Pydantic.
  • Key Modules:
  • zuhura_data.spatial.alignment: Alignment of MOLA MEG128, CTX, and HiRISE grids.
  • zuhura_data.terrain.quantized_mesh: Generation of quantized-mesh terrain tiles for Cesium.
  • zuhura_data.catalog: STAC item and collection metadata builder.
  • Strengths: Robust validation test suite (33 tests); strict check on NoData values and nodata masking.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • True Resolution Accounting: Tile metadata does not always distinguish nominal camera ground sample distance (GSD) from effective spatial resolution degraded by atmospheric dust or compression.
  • Data Checksums: Checksums (SHA-256) are defined in manifests but not continuously validated during runtime ingestion.

docs.title: 3.4 Repository: zuhura-api
docs.text:
• Primary Role: Canonical contract definitions for OpenAPI, JSON Schemas, and STAC extensions.
  • Tech Stack: OpenAPI 3.1.0, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12.
  • Key Assets:
  • openapi/zuhura-v1.yaml: Complete REST API contract definitions.
  • schemas/: Schemas for spatial queries, AI queries, datasets, and terrain analysis.
  • stac/mars-stac-extension.json: STAC extension specifying planetary coordinate systems, vertical areoid datum, and lighting conditions ($L_s$).
  • Strengths: Strict contract-first design; eliminates API drift between backend and frontend.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • Lacks automated schemathesis / tavern contract-compliance testing in CI pipeline to verify live endpoints against OpenAPI definitions.

docs.title: 3.5 Repository: zuhura-docs
docs.text:
• Primary Role: System architecture documentation, mathematical specifications, geodesy guidelines, operational reports.
  • Tech Stack: MkDocs Material, Markdown, Mermaid, MathJax.
  • Key Sections:
  • Geodetic standards (IAU 2015 WGCCRE, MOLA areoid).
  • AI methodology and epistemic grounding tags.
  • Historical execution and baseline reports.
  • Strengths: Clear mathematical formulations and references to peer-reviewed literature.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • Needs real-time synchronization with newly developed endpoints, provenance schemas, and researcher workspace features.

docs.title: 3.6 Repository: zuhura (Root Orchestration)
docs.text:
• Primary Role: System orchestration, container definitions, environment configuration, database bootstrapping.
  • Tech Stack: Docker Compose, PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS, Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared).
  • Key Assets:
  • docker/docker-compose.yml: Multi-container service definitions.
  • docker/init-db.sql: Database schema initialization.
  • Strengths: Clean separation of microservices.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • Dockerfile configurations run as root in several build stages; should be hardened to non-privileged user.
  • PostgreSQL lacks automated backup cron and volume backup verification.

docs.title: 3.7 Repository: .github
docs.text:
• Primary Role: Organization-wide governance, CI/CD pipeline, issue and pull request templates.
  • Tech Stack: GitHub Actions, YAML.
  • Key Workflows:
  • ci.yml: Unified CI running ruff, pytest (backend & data), typecheck, vitest (frontend), and schema validation.
  • Strengths: Covers linting, testing, and schema validation in a single pipeline.
  • Weaknesses & Identified Issues:
  • Frontend step uses npm run typecheck || true allowing potential type errors to pass quietly.
  • Missing container security vulnerability scanning (Trivy / Grype) and automated dependency auditing.

docs.title: 3. Detailed Breakdown of New Features Implemented
3.1 X-Ray Mars (Planetary Interior Engine)
docs.text:
• Scientific Foundation: Modeled using NASA InSight SEIS data (Knapmeyer-Endrun et al. 2021, Khan et al. 2021, Stähler et al. 2021, Samuel et al. 2023).
  • Physical Layers Modeled:
  • Upper Crust: 0–10 km, fractured basaltic regolith, density 2,600 kg/m³, $V_p = 2.8$ km/s, $V_s = 1.6$ km/s.
  • Middle Crust: 10–25 km, altered basalt, density 2,850 kg/m³, $V_p = 4.5$ km/s, $V_s = 2.5$ km/s.
  • Lower Crust: 25–45 km, dense mafic granulite/gabbro, density 3,100 kg/m³, $V_p = 6.2$ km/s, $V_s = 3.6$ km/s.
  • Lithospheric Mantle: 45–500 km, cold depleted peridotite, density 3,450 kg/m³, $V_p = 7.9$ km/s, $V_s = 4.4$ km/s.
  • Upper Mantle & Transition Zone: 500–1,050 km, olivine-wadsleyite-ringwoodite, density 3,700 kg/m³, $V_p = 8.6$ km/s, $V_s = 4.8$ km/s.
  • Lower Mantle: 1,050–1,570 km, bridgmanite and ferropericlase, density 4,100 kg/m³, $V_p = 9.8$ km/s, $V_s = 5.4$ km/s.
  • CMB Molten Silicate Slag Layer: 1,570–1,720 km, basal magma ocean remnant, density 4,400 kg/m³, $V_p = 7.2$ km/s, $V_s = 2.9$ km/s.
  • Liquid Outer Core: 1,720–3,396 km (radius $1,570 \pm 30$ km), liquid Fe-Ni-S-C-O alloy, density 6,100–7,100 kg/m³, $V_p = 5.1$ km/s, $V_s = 0.0$ km/s.
  • Crustal Dichotomy: Asymmetry modeled with Northern Lowlands average crustal thickness of 32 km vs Southern Highlands 58 km.
  • Frontend Component: src/components/XRayMarsModal.tsx provides an interactive SVG polar cutaway with adjustable angle slider (0°–180°), layer selection HUD, seismic velocity graphs, and crustal dichotomy comparison tabs.

docs.title: 3.2 Optimize Navigation (Terrain-Aware Routing)
docs.text:
• Pathfinding Algorithm: Geodesic grid A* search with 8-connectivity over MOLA MEG128 digital elevation models.
  • Cost Formulation: $$C(p_1, p_2) = D(p_1, p_2) \cdot \left(1.0 + 2.5 \cdot \left(\frac{\theta}{\theta_{\max}}\right)^2 + 1.2 \cdot \frac{\text{TRI}}{50.0}\right)$$ Where $D$ is the great-circle arc length on the IAU biaxial ellipsoid, $\theta$ is the topographic slope in degrees, $\theta_{\max}$ is the vehicle's maximum climb limit, and $\text{TRI}$ is Riley's Terrain Ruggedness Index.
  • Vehicle Mobility Profiles:
  • Perseverance / Curiosity Class: Max slope 25°, max step 0.35m, energy penalty 1.2, speed 0.12 km/h.
  • Scout / Fast Rover: Max slope 30°, max step 0.25m, energy penalty 0.9, speed 0.35 km/h.
  • Heavy Cargo / Habitat Transporter: Max slope 15°, max step 0.20m, energy penalty 2.0, speed 0.08 km/h.
  • Pressurized Crew Rover: Max slope 20°, max step 0.40m, energy penalty 1.5, speed 0.25 km/h.
  • Frontend Component: src/components/RoutePlanningDrawer.tsx includes preset exploration scenarios (Jezero Delta Traverse, Gale Mount Sharp Ascent, Valles Marineris Floor, Olympus Mons Rim), vehicle selector, SVG profile drawer with cumulative climb, and one-click GeoJSON export.
  • Globe Integration: Glowing 3D Cesium polyline rendered on the terrain surface.

docs.title: 3.3 Hover Intelligence (Contextual Telemetry HUD)
docs.text:
• Performance: High-efficiency spatial inspection with 200ms debounce and in-memory LRU spatial coordinate cache rounded to 0.001° (~59m ground distance).
  • HUD Telemetry Points:
  • Planetographic Latitude & Longitude (IAU/IAG 2015 WGCCRE).
  • Surface Elevation against MOLA Areoid datum (meters).
  • Nearest IAU Named Feature with morphological classification and proximity.
  • Regional Geological Unit and dominant mineralogy.
  • Solar Illumination status (Solar Longitude $L_s$, local solar time, sub-solar incidence).
  • Active Sensor Resolution tier (Viking, CTX, or HiRISE).
  • Frontend Component: src/components/HoverIntelligenceTooltip.tsx floating HUD card tracking mouse pointer with toggle button in Header.

docs.title: 3.4 Location Pinpoint (Computer Vision Terrain Localization)
docs.text:
• Vision Algorithm: Two-stage morphological terrain matching:
  • Gradient Edge Feature Extraction: Laplacian variance edge density analyzing bedrock stratification vs smooth regolith.
  • Normalized Brightness Histogram Correlation: 16-bin optical density profile matched against reference Martian surface rover stations.
  • Mission Context Prior: Bayesian spatial weighting when mission context (Perseverance, Curiosity, Opportunity, Spirit) is specified.
  • Ground Truth Reference Sites: Jezero Crater Delta Front, Jezero Octavia E. Butler Landing, Gale Crater Mount Sharp, Gale Bradbury Landing, Meridiani Planum Eagle Crater, Gusev Crater Columbia Memorial Station, Valles Marineris Candor Chasma, Olympus Mons Caldera.
  • Security & Integrity: 10MB payload ceiling, magic number image header validation (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp), and sandboxed memory handling.
  • Frontend Component: src/components/LocationPinpointModal.tsx drag-and-drop image dropzone with candidate confidence rankings and "Fly to Location" Cesium camera transition.

docs.title: 3.5 Mars Region Discovery Engine
docs.text:

  • Topological Validity: Emits valid closed GeoJSON polygons ($P_0 = P_n$) with verified winding order.
  • Provisional Nomenclature Standard: Every generated candidate region is strictly tagged with:
  • naming_authority: "PROVISIONAL_PLATFORM_GENERATED"
  • iau_status: "UNOFFICIAL_CANDIDATE"
  • Disclaimer: "Provisional autonomous region segmentation for scientific exploration only. Not approved by IAU WGPSN."
  • Frontend Component: src/components/RegionDiscoveryPanel.tsx with adjustable segmentation radius slider (25–250 km), unit cards, Cesium polygon overlay rendering, and GeoJSON export.

docs.title: 5.1 Planetary Geodesy & Reference Datums
docs.text:
• Ellipsoid Parameters: Conforms strictly to IAU/IAG 2015 WGCCRE recommendations:
  • Semi-major axis ($a$): $3,396,190.0\text{ m}$
  • Semi-minor axis ($b$): $3,376,200.0\text{ m}$
  • Flattening ($f$): $\frac{a - b}{a} = 0.005886$
  • Elevation Datum: MOLA Areoid equipotential gravity surface defined by spherical harmonics (GMM-2B/GMM-3).
  • Coordinate Conventions: Planetographic latitude (north positive) and positive East longitude ($0^\circ - 360^\circ$ and $-180^\circ - +180^\circ$).

docs.title: 5.2 Seismological Interior Structure
docs.text:
• Crustal layering grounded in receiver function analysis from InSight event S1222a and ambient seismic noise.
  • Liquid iron-nickel-sulfur-carbon core with radius $1,570 \pm 30\text{ km}$, bounded by a $\sim 150\text{ km}$ thick basal molten silicate layer ("slag") explaining P-wave travel time delays (Samuel et al., Nature 2023).

docs.title: 5.3 Martian Solar Chronometry
docs.text:
• Solar Longitude ($L_s$): Computed from J2000 Martian orbital ephemeris.
  • Sub-solar latitude: $\delta_s = \arcsin(\sin \epsilon \cdot \sin L_s)$, where $\epsilon = 25.19^\circ$ is Martian obliquity.
  • Local Solar Incidence: $\cos \theta_i = \sin \phi \sin \delta_s + \cos \phi \cos \delta_s \cos(\text{LST} \cdot 15^\circ - 180^\circ)$.

docs.title: 9. AI Assistant Tool Definitions and Capabilities
docs.text:
The MarsAIScientist tool registry (src/zuhura/ai/tools.py) was extended with 5 deterministic tools:

  1. get_mars_interior_structure: Inspects InSight seismic layering, core radius, crustal dichotomy, and physical density profiles.
  2. optimize_navigation_route: Calculates optimal terrain-aware paths across MOLA DEM given vehicle constraints.
  3. inspect_hover_location: Queries multi-sensor surface telemetry, solar incidence, and geodetic elevation for any point on Mars.
  4. pinpoint_mars_landscape_image: Analyzes terrain images against ground truth rover stations using computer vision.
  5. discover_geological_regions: Segments candidate geological units with closed polygon geometry and provisional designations.

All tools include strict JSON schema parameter validation and unit test coverage in test_mars_ai_scientist.py.

docs.title: 10. Architectural Decisions and Patterns Followed
docs.text:
1. Additive Router Injection: New backend endpoints are encapsulated in dedicated modules (src/zuhura/api/v1/*.py) and included via app.include_router(prefix="/api/v1"), preventing any alteration to existing core routes.
  2. Typed GIS Client Layer: Added src/lib/advancedApiClient.ts in zuhura-frontend providing strongly typed TypeScript interfaces for all responses, preventing runtime type mismatches.
  3. Graceful GDAL Fallback: Navigation routing and hover telemetry utilize high-resolution MOLA MEG128 GeoTIFFs when available, falling back smoothly to bilinearly interpolated MEG016 or mathematical areoid models if outside tile bounds.
  4. Isolated State Slices: Extended Zustand state stores (globeStore.ts) without modifying existing selector hooks used by pre-existing components.

docs.title: 11. Security Measures Implemented
docs.text:
• Image Upload Constraints: LocationPinpoint limits uploads to 10 MB, enforces allowed extensions (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .webp, .tif), and validates initial magic bytes.
  • Path Traversal Defenses: All file lookups resolve through canonical paths within DATA_REPO_ROOT, preventing arbitrary directory access.
  • Zero Secret Exposure: .gitignore files verified across all repositories; .env and API keys are strictly excluded from git tracking.
  • Sanitized Coordinate Inputs: Latitudes constrained to $[-90.0, +90.0]$ and longitudes to $[-180.0, +360.0]$ with modulo wrapping.

docs.title: 12. Performance Optimizations and Benchmark Results
docs.text:
• Spatial Caching: Hover telemetry uses an LRU cache with spatial key rounding ($0.001^\circ$), resulting in $O(1)$ response times ($<2\text{ ms}$) for repeated hover movements over the same region.
  • A Pathfinder Geodesic Heuristic: The A router uses Great-Circle distance on the reference ellipsoid as an admissible heuristic, pruning $>85\%$ of the search space compared to Dijkstra.
  • Frontend Bundle Size: Production build (vite build) completes in 2.52 seconds, outputting a gzipped JavaScript bundle of only 78.28 kB and CSS of 6.39 kB.

docs.title: 21. Route Planning Algorithm Details and Vehicle Profiles
docs.text:
• Grid Resolution: 128 samples per degree ($\approx 463\text{ m}$ per cell).
  • Slope Calculation: 2nd-order central difference gradient over local $3 \times 3$ MOLA elevation kernel.
  • Cost Minimization: Dijkstra/A* evaluation minimizing total energy consumption factoring incline, surface roughness, and vehicle climbing threshold.
  • GeoJSON Output: Compliant Feature<LineString> with point elevation telemetry and cumulative climb metrics.

docs.title: 22. Computer Vision Landscape Matching Methodology
docs.text:
• Input Normalization: Ingested Martian landscape images are resized to a standard $512 \times 512$ monochrome intensity matrix.
  • Laplacian Edge Variance: Measures structural topography and rock density: $$\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{N} \sum (L(x, y) - \mu)^2$$
  • Histogram Density: Computes 16-bin normalized brightness histogram to distinguish bright dust deposits from dark basalt sand.
  • Distance Metric: Combined L1 histogram distance and edge variance delta matched against calibrated rover panoramas.

docs.title: 25.1 High-DPI Resolution & Surface Clarity (Without Additional Datasets)
docs.text:
• Problem: Default Cesium canvas defaulted to a 1:1 CSS pixel ratio, resulting in blurry, sub-sampled rendering on Retina and 4K displays; furthermore, default ground atmospheric fog washed out surface relief.
  • Solution:
  • viewer.resolutionScale = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1.0, 2.0) eliminates pixelation on high-DPI displays.
  • globe.maximumScreenSpaceError = 0.8 (down from 1.33) forces immediate loading of highest-detail mipmap levels.
  • scene.msaaSamples = 4 enables multi-sample anti-aliasing for razor-sharp crater rims and ridge lines.
  • globe.showGroundAtmosphere = false removes atmospheric wash, revealing pristine surface contrast.
  • Linear mipmap texture filtering (LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR) applied across Viking (232m), CTX (5.55m), and HiRISE (0.50m) tile pyramids.

docs.title: 25.2 Dynamic Real-Time Hover Intelligence Engine
docs.text:
• Problem: Mouse hover needed to immediately display an informative description of the exact Martian landmark or region and continuously change as the cursor moves across different craters, volcanoes, and plains.
  • Solution:
  • Embedded 78 official IAU nomenclature landmarks and 18 regional provinces client-side in zuhura-frontend/src/lib/hoverData.ts.
  • Implemented zero-latency synchronous lookup getHoverPlaceDescription(lat, lon, elev) paired with debounced asynchronous backend enrichment (zuhura-backend/src/zuhura/api/v1/hover.py).
  • Cursor movement dynamically switches between crater descriptions (e.g. Gale, Jezero, Korolev), volcanic calderas (Olympus Mons, Ascraeus Mons), canyon systems (Valles Marineris), and regional geological units (Elysium Planitia, Tharsis Rise).

docs.title: 25.3 Interactive Pinpoint Departure & Arrival Navigation
docs.text:
• Problem: Direct click-to-pinpoint navigation was needed where clicking on the 3D globe allows the user to pinpoint a departure location (Start) and an arrival destination (Target), then immediately draw and calculate the optimal traverse route across the terrain.
  • Solution:
  • State machine in zuhura-frontend/src/store/globeStore.ts: select_departure $\rightarrow$ select_arrival $\rightarrow$ routing $\rightarrow$ route_ready.
  • Interactive Cesium left-click raycasting picks terrain coordinates:
    • Click 1: Drops animated emerald Departure Pin with elevation readout.
    • Click 2: Drops glowing ruby Arrival Pin, calculates route using A* traversal or client-side great-circle slerp with MOLA elevation sampling, and renders glowing 3D polyline corridor on terrain.
  • PinpointRouteHUD.tsx floating HUD displays travel sols, distance (km), vertical climb (m), rover vehicle profiles, and GeoJSON export.
  • "Photo Match" preserved as a dedicated tool for Martian landscape photo localization.

docs.title: 25.4 True 3D Navigable X-Ray Mars Interior Model
docs.text:
• Problem: X-Ray Mars interior needed to be a fully interactive, exact 3D planetary model that users can navigate (rotate, zoom, pan, orbit) just like the real globe.
  • Solution:
  • Built zuhura-frontend/src/components/XRayMars3DModal.tsx using Three.js and OrbitControls.
  • Full 3D camera navigation: left-click orbit drag, middle-click pan, scroll wheel smooth zoom from planetary orbit down to the metallic core.
  • Concentric 3D cutaway shells based on published NASA InSight seismic data:
    • Crust (0–45 km) with procedural crater relief and polar ice caps.
    • Lithospheric Mantle (45–500 km, olivine/pyroxene).
    • Lower Mantle (500–1,570 km, bridgmanite/ringwoodite).
    • Basal Molten Silicate Slag Layer (1,570–1,720 km, Samuel et al. Nature 2023).
    • Liquid Fe-Ni-S Core ($R = 1,570\text{ km}$, Stähler et al. Science 2021).
  • Dynamic cutaway angle slider ($0^\circ - 180^\circ$), exploded layer separation slider, interactive 3D raycast layer inspection with telemetry HUD, and animated seismic wave ray paths (P & S waves).

docs.text: Document Identifier: ZUHURA_SCI_VAL_2026_V1 Execution Date: 2026-11-13 Status: APPROVED & RIGOROUSLY VALIDATED Authors: Senior Planetary Scientist, Planetary Geologist, Geodesy & Remote Sensing Specialist Target Repositories: All 7 Zuhura Repositories

docs.title: 1. Scope & Scientific Mandate
docs.text:
Planetary digital twins often suffer from "visual realism over scientific truth," where aesthetic rendering conceals incorrect coordinate conversions, undocumented elevation datums, speculative planetary interior models, or synthetic confidence scores.

The primary directive of this report is to enforce Scientific Truth: 1. Prove what is correct against empirical peer-reviewed literature. 2. Resolve scientific inconsistencies across the planetary interior model. 3. Establish a formal scientific classification taxonomy (OBSERVED, MEASURED, DERIVED, MODEL_ESTIMATED, SIMULATED, PROVISIONAL, UNVERIFIED). 4. Validate geodetic coordinates against IAU/IAG Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements (WGCCRE 2015). 5. Document all modeling uncertainties, empirical boundary conditions, and literature citations.

docs.title: 2.1 The Reference Ellipsoid
docs.text: All geospatial computations within Zuhura are referenced to the IAU/IAG 2015 WGCCRE biaxial reference ellipsoid: - Equatorial Semi-Major Axis ($A$): $3,396,190.0\text{ m}$ ($3,396.190\text{ km}$) - Polar Semi-Minor Axis ($C$): $3,376,200.0\text{ m}$ ($3,376.200\text{ km}$) - Flattening ($f$): $$f = \frac{A - C}{A} = \frac{3,396,190 - 3,376,200}{3,396,190} = \frac{19,990}{3,396,190} \approx \frac{1}{169.89445}$$ - First Eccentricity Squared ($e^2$): $$e^2 = 2f - f^2 = 1 - \frac{C^2}{A^2} \approx 0.0117079$$

docs.title: 2.2 Latitude Definitions
docs.text:
• Planetocentric Latitude ($\phi_c$): Angle between the equatorial plane and the vector from the planetary center to the surface point.
  • Planetographic Latitude ($\phi_g$): Angle between the equatorial plane and the local surface normal vector.
  • Conversion Equation: $$\tan(\phi_c) = (1 - f)^2 \tan(\phi_g) = \left(\frac{C}{A}\right)^2 \tan(\phi_g) \approx 0.988292 \cdot \tan(\phi_g)$$
  • Standard Enforced: Planetocentric latitude $[-90.0^\circ, +90.0^\circ]$ is the internal canonical standard for all database, calculation, and API representations. Planetographic latitude is provided strictly as a selectable display conversion.

docs.title: 2.3 Longitude Conventions
docs.text:
• Internal and API standard: East-Positive Longitude in the range $[0.0^\circ, 360.0^\circ]$ or $[-180.0^\circ, +180.0^\circ]$.
  • Normalization algorithm: $$\lambda_{\text{norm}} = ((\lambda \pmod{360.0}) + 360.0) \pmod{360.0}$$

docs.title: 2.4 Vertical Datum (Areoid)
docs.text:
• Topographic Datum: Mars Areoid defined by the MOLA GMM-3 / MEG128 spherical harmonic equipotential reference surface.
  • Mean equatorial radius at the areoid: $3,396,000\text{ m}$.
  • Every elevation value $z$ in Zuhura represents the metric height above the local areoid, never an arbitrary distance from the planetary center or an optical brightness proxy.

docs.title: 3. Mars Interior Geophysics: Comprehensive Synthesis & InSight SEIS Reconciliation
3.1 Historical Context & Published Discrepancy
docs.text:
Between 2021 and 2023, data from the NASA InSight SEIS (Seismic Experiment for Interior Structure) instrument transformed understanding of the Martian interior. However, initial 2021 publications and subsequent 2023 discoveries contained significant discrepancies that must be reconciled in the digital twin:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                  INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED MODELS                                          |
+====================================+==================================+================================+
| Parameter                          | Stähler et al. (Science 2021)    | Samuel & Khan (Nature 2023)    |
+------------------------------------+----------------------------------+--------------------------------+
| Moho Depth (Elysium Planitia)      | 20-39 km (2-layer) / 72 km (3-ly)| 39 ± 8 km                      |
| Lithospheric Mantle Thickness      | ~400-500 km                      | ~450 km                        |
| Convective Mantle Bottom           | 1,560 km depth (Core interface)  | 1,520 km depth (Slag top)      |
| Basal Molten Silicate Slag Layer   | NOT IDENTIFIED (Absent in model) | 1,520 - 1,680 km (160 km thick)|
| Core Radius                        | 1,830 ± 40 km (Large core)       | 1,650 ± 20 km (Revised core)   |
| Core Bulk Density                  | 5,700 - 6,300 kg/m³              | 6,100 - 6,400 kg/m³            |
| Core Light-Element Fraction        | > 20 wt% (Difficult to reconcile)| 15 - 18 wt% (S, C, O, H)       |
| Core State                         | Fully Liquid (Vs = 0 km/s)       | Fully Liquid (Vs = 0 km/s)     |
+------------------------------------+----------------------------------+--------------------------------+

docs.title: 3.2 The Basal Molten Silicate Layer Discovery (Nature 2023)
docs.text: In October 2023, two independent papers (Samuel et al. and Khan et al.) re-analyzed seismic data from a meteorite impact on the far side of Mars (event S1000a) and high-frequency diffracted shear waves ($P_{\text{diff}}$ and $SKS$). - The Breakthrough: The sharp seismic reflection previously interpreted as the core-mantle boundary at $R = 1,830\text{ km}$ was actually the top of a deep, completely molten silicate slag layer (150–170 km thick). - Physical Consequence: The true liquid iron-nickel core sits underneath this molten silicate layer with a reduced radius of $1,650 \pm 20\text{ km}$. - Thermodynamic Impact: The basal silicate blanket is enriched in radioactive elements (potassium, thorium, uranium), which insulated the metallic core and delayed the collapse of the early Martian dynamo.

docs.text:

  • Radius: $1,650 \pm 20\text{ km}$ (Reconciled from 2021 estimate of $1,830\text{ km}$)
  • Density: $6,100\text{ kg/m}^3$ (Uncertainty: $5,800 - 6,400$)
  • Seismic Velocities: $V_p = 5.1\text{ km/s}$, $V_s = 0.0\text{ km/s}$ (Complete extinction of shear wave confirms liquid state)
  • Evidence Type: MEASURED (Direct core reflections and SKS travel time records)
  • Composition: Molten Fe-Ni with 15–18 wt% Sulfur, plus minor Carbon, Oxygen, Hydrogen
  • Inner Core: Currently UNVERIFIED; no seismic wave phase ($PKIKP$) has been confirmed to reflect from a solid inner core boundary.
  • Citation: Stähler et al. (2021), Science 373(6553), 443-448; Irving et al. (2023), PNAS 120(18)

docs.title: 4. Scientific Epistemic Classification Framework
docs.text:
To eliminate scientific ambiguity, every piece of telemetry, spatial data, and AI analysis emitted by Zuhura must be labeled with an explicit classification:

  +------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                           SCIENTIFIC CLASSIFICATION TAXONOMY                       |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Tag              | Definition & Application Requirement                            |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | OBSERVED         | Direct physical observation from calibrated instrument sensors. |
  |                  | Examples: Calibrated CTX/HiRISE optical pixels, Viking albedo.  |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | MEASURED         | Derived directly from instrument metrics via physical laws.     |
  |                  | Examples: MOLA laser pulse transit time areoid elevation,      |
  |                  | InSight SEIS seismogram arrival times.                          |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | DERIVED          | Computed using verified mathematical transforms on measured data|
  |                  | Examples: Horn 1981 slope gradients, aspect, TRI roughness.     |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | MODEL_ESTIMATED  | Produced via physical or geodynamic models with uncertainties.  |
  |                  | Examples: Mantle density profile, thermal lithosphere thickness.|
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | SIMULATED        | Synthetic scenario or path computation.                         |
  |                  | Examples: A* rover traverse route, travel sol estimates.        |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | PROVISIONAL      | Automated preliminary hypothesis requiring peer validation.     |
  |                  | Examples: Machine-discovered candidate geological units.        |
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
  | UNVERIFIED       | Insufficient evidence or conflicting literature.                 |
  |                  | Examples: Existence of Martian solid inner core, deep ice depth.|
  +------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: ZUHURA MARS — COMPREHENSIVE SECURITY & DEVSECOPS AUDIT
docs.text: Document Identifier: ZUHURA_SEC_AUDIT_2026_V1 Execution Date: 2026-11-13 Status: ACTIVE / HARDENING IN PROGRESS Authors: Lead DevSecOps Engineer, Cybersecurity Architect, Cloud Security Lead Scope: All 7 Zuhura Repositories and Orchestration Stack

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: This security audit assesses the risk posture across the Zuhura Mars platform. The platform processes geospatial data, executes terrain analysis algorithms, interfaces with AI large language models, and delivers high-performance 3D WebGL visualization.

docs.title: Key Audit Highlights:
docs.text:
• Git Credential & Secret Hygiene: Verified that no private tokens, passwords, or cloud credentials are hardcoded into source control or committed .env files.
  • Backend API Hardening: Input validation is enforced via Pydantic schemas; however, rate limiting and fine-grained CORS domain restrictions must be strictly enforced for production.
  • Container Security: The backend Dockerfile executes as a non-privileged user (USER 1000); the frontend Dockerfile currently defaults to Node.js dev server and should be hardened to a non-root static production image.
  • Raster Path Traversal Protection: File paths passed to GDAL/Rasterio engines are sandboxed within DATA_REPO_ROOT, preventing arbitrary filesystem reads (/etc/passwd, host volumes).
  • AI Tool Execution Boundaries: The AI tool registry strictly validates parameters using Pydantic schemas, isolating LLM hallucinated parameters from direct shell execution.

docs.text: Threat Category Target Component Risk Level Current Mitigation Hardening Requirement Path Traversal Raster & DEM APIs (/api/v1/rasters/sample) HIGH Paths are resolved against settings.DATA_REPO_ROOT Add canonical path verification to ensure paths cannot escape via .. docs.title: 3.1 Backend Application (zuhura-backend)
docs.text:
• Framework: FastAPI with Uvicorn.
  • Input Validation: Pydantic v2 schemas rigorously check numeric ranges (e.g., latitude $[-90, 90]$, longitude $[-180, 360]$) and kernel sizes ($3, 5, 7$).
  • Raster File Access:
  • Vulnerability: Unchecked raster_id query parameters could potentially traverse directory structures.
  • Audit Finding: zuhura.core.config.settings.DATA_REPO_ROOT is prepended to relative paths.
  • Recommendation: Explicitly verify that resolved_path.is_relative_to(settings.DATA_REPO_ROOT) before opening with GDAL.
  • Authentication & Authorization:
  • Public endpoints serve scientific open data.
  • Research session creation and management should support session tokens / JWT headers for multi-user research isolation.

docs.title: 3.2 Frontend Application (zuhura-frontend)
docs.text:
• Framework: Vite + React 18.
  • Dependencies: Lucide React, Cesium, Three.js, Zustand.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria and Verification Specifications
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Phase: Stage 8 Phase 1 (Acceptance Specifications) Status: PROPOSED / PENDING APPROVAL Platform: Zuhura Integrated Planetary Digital Twin Verification Method: Automated Pytest Integration + Headless Selenium Visual Acceptance

docs.title: 1. Acceptance Framework Overview
docs.text:
Stage 8 acceptance requires passing all 10 verification test suites defined below. Testing encompasses mathematical correctness, geodetic precision, boundary safety, provenance transparency, performance latency, and interactive frontend visual rendering.

A test is classified as PASSED only when automated verification confirms numerical results within defined physical tolerances and visual evidence verifies distortion-free rendering.

docs.title: Suite 1: Geodetic & Coordinate Transformations (AC-01)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Compliance with IAU/IAG 2015 Mars Biaxial Ellipsoid ($A = 3,396,190\text{ m}$, $C = 3,376,200\text{ m}$).
  • Test Cases:
  • Planetographic to Planetocentric Latitude Conversion:
    • At Equator ($0^\circ$): $\Delta \phi = 0.0^\circ$ ($< 10^{-6\circ}$).
    • At Poles ($\pm 90^\circ$): $\Delta \phi = 0.0^\circ$ ($< 10^{-6\circ}$).
    • At $\phi = 45.0^\circ$: Correctly calculates planetocentric latitude $\phi_c \approx 44.6626^\circ$ ($\Delta \phi \approx 0.3374^\circ$, corresponding to $\approx 20.4\text{ km}$ physical displacement).
  • Longitude Normalization:
    • Negative longitudes (e.g. $-59.2^\circ$) normalize to $[0, 360)$ East ($300.8^\circ\text{E}$).
    • Values $\ge 360^\circ$ wrap correctly (e.g. $437.58^\circ \rightarrow 77.58^\circ\text{E}$).
  • Great-Circle Distance Verification:
    • Distance between $(0^\circ\text{N}, 0^\circ\text{E})$ and $(0^\circ\text{N}, 90^\circ\text{E})$ on Mars equals $\frac{\pi}{2} \times 3,389.5\text{ km} \approx 5,324.22\text{ km}$ ($\pm 0.5\text{ km}$).

docs.title: Suite 2: Known Elevation Reference Points & Datum Accuracy (AC-02)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Point elevations query directly from MOLA GMM-3 areoid datum without synthetic interpolation bias.
  • Reference Landmark Verification Matrix: | Landmark | Target Latitude | Target Longitude | Expected Elevation Range (Areoid) | Expected Result | Tolerance | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | Olympus Mons Summit | $18.65^\circ\text{N}$ | $226.20^\circ\text{E}$ | $+20,000\text{ m}$ to $+21,250\text{ m}$ | $+20,015\text{ m}$ to $+21,249\text{ m}$ | $\pm 10\text{ m}$ | | Jezero Crater Floor | $18.38^\circ\text{N}$ | $77.58^\circ\text{E}$ | $-2,700\text{ m}$ to $-2,550\text{ m}$ | $-2,648\text{ m}$ | $\pm 5\text{ m}$ | | Gale Crater (Curiosity Landing)| $-5.37^\circ\text{N}$ | $137.81^\circ\text{E}$ | $-4,550\text{ m}$ to $-4,400\text{ m}$ | $-4,503\text{ m}$ | $\pm 5\text{ m}$ | | Valles Marineris Floor | $-13.90^\circ\text{N}$ | $300.80^\circ\text{E}$ | $-5,600\text{ m}$ to $-5,400\text{ m}$ | $-5,511\text{ m}$ | $\pm 10\text{ m}$ | | Hellas Planitia Basin Floor | $-42.50^\circ\text{N}$ | $70.50^\circ\text{E}$ | $-8,250\text{ m}$ to $-8,000\text{ m}$ | $\le -8,100\text{ m}$ | $\pm 10\text{ m}$ | | Areoid Zero-Datum Plain | Variable | Variable | Near $0\text{ m}$ | Zero-crossing confirmed | $\pm 2\text{ m}$ |

docs.title: Suite 3: Slope and Aspect Derivative Calculations (AC-03)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Slope and aspect correctly computed using the Metric Latitude-Scaled Horn $3\times 3$ operator.
  • Test Cases:
  • Synthetic Planar Ramp Test:
    • Feed a synthetic $3\times 3$ grid with a known physical gradient (e.g. $10.0^\circ, 30.0^\circ, 45.0^\circ$).
    • Calculated slope must match true slope to within $\pm 0.01^\circ$.
  • Aspect Directionality Test:
    • North-dipping ramp: Aspect $= 0.0^\circ$ ($\pm 0.1^\circ$).
    • East-dipping ramp: Aspect $= 90.0^\circ$ ($\pm 0.1^\circ$).
    • South-dipping ramp: Aspect $= 180.0^\circ$ ($\pm 0.1^\circ$).
    • West-dipping ramp: Aspect $= 270.0^\circ$ ($\pm 0.1^\circ$).
  • Latitudinal Metric Tensor Scaling Test:
    • Compute slope on an east-west gradient at Equator ($0^\circ\text{N}$) and at high latitude ($75^\circ\text{N}$).
    • The calculation must account for $\Delta x = \Delta x_0 \cos(75^\circ) \approx 0.2588 \times \Delta x_0$.
    • Unscaled algorithm will underestimate slope by $386\%$; scaled algorithm must produce the correct physical gradient within $\pm 0.1\%$.
  • Flat Surface Handling:
    • Surface with zero elevation gradient returns slope_deg: 0.0, aspect_deg: null, is_flat: true.

docs.title: Suite 4: Terrain Transect & Geodesic Profiling (AC-04)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Elevation profile sampled along great-circle arc with monotonic distance accumulation.
  • Test Cases:
  • Distance Monotonicity:
    • For all samples $i \in [1, N-1]$: $d_i > d_{i-1}$ and $d_{N-1} = D_{\text{total}} \pm 0.001\text{ km}$.
  • Endpoint Elevation Fidelity:
    • $z(d_0)$ matches point elevation query at $P_1$ ($\pm 0.1\text{ m}$).
    • $z(d_{N-1})$ matches point elevation query at $P_2$ ($\pm 0.1\text{ m}$).
  • Real Planetary Transect Verification:
    • Transect across Jezero Western Delta fan (length $\approx 30\text{ km}$):
    • Resolves delta front scarp drop $> 100\text{ m}$.
    • Peak slope along scarp $> 10^\circ$.
    • Transect across Valles Marineris canyon chasma (length $\approx 200\text{ km}$):
    • Total relief $> 5,000\text{ m}$.
    • Wall slopes $> 20^\circ$.

docs.title: Suite 5: Local Morphometry & Kernel Statistics (AC-05)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Focal kernel metrics accurately differentiate smooth plains from rugged crater terrain.
  • Test Cases:
  • Isidis Planitia (Smooth Plain):
    • TRI $< 10.0\text{ m}$.
    • Local relief $< 25.0\text{ m}$.
    • TPI class: "flat_plain".
  • Jezero Crater Rim (Rugged Scarp):
    • TRI $> 40.0\text{ m}$.
    • Local relief $> 200.0\text{ m}$.
    • TPI class: "ridge" or "upper_slope".
  • Kernel Size Scaling:
    • Supported kernel sizes: $3\times 3$, $5\times 5$, $7\times 7$. Non-supported sizes (e.g. 4) return HTTP 400.

docs.title: Suite 6: Spatial Comparison Endpoint (AC-06)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Accurate differential analysis between two distinct planetary sites.
  • Test Cases:
  • Separation Distance: Great-circle distance between Jezero ($18.38^\circ\text{N}, 77.58^\circ\text{E}$) and Gale ($-5.37^\circ\text{N}, 137.81^\circ\text{E}$) equals $3,842.15\text{ km} \pm 10\text{ km}$.
  • Elevation Delta: $\Delta z = z_{\text{Gale}} - z_{\text{Jezero}} = -4,503 - (-2,648) = -1,855\text{ m}$ ($\pm 5\text{ m}$).
  • Comparative Output: Response returns side-by-side table of elevation, slope, aspect, and roughness.

docs.title: Suite 7: Boundary & NoData Handling (AC-07)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Safe, graceful handling of coordinate boundaries and edge cases.
  • Test Cases:
  • Equatorial Coverage Boundary ($|\phi| \le 88.0^\circ$): Served via global MOLA COG v3 (nodata_status: false).
  • Polar Boundary ($|\phi| > 88.0^\circ$): Automatically routes to Polar Stereographic DEM (megt_n_128_1.tif or megt_s_128_1.tif) with explicit CRS metadata in response.
  • Antimeridian Crossing ($180^\circ\text{E}$): Transect profiles traversing $180^\circ\text{E}$ sample smoothly without index out-of-range exceptions.
  • Prime Meridian Crossing ($0^\circ / 360^\circ\text{E}$): Profile traversing from $359^\circ\text{E}$ to $1^\circ\text{E}$ computes shortest distance arc ($2^\circ$), not $358^\circ$ retrograde arc.
  • Invalid Inputs: Latitude $> 90^\circ$ or $<-90^\circ$ returns HTTP 422 / 400.

docs.title: Suite 8: Scientific Provenance & Uncertainty Reporting (AC-08)
docs.text:
• Requirement: Complete metadata transparency in every response payload.
  • Verification Criteria:
  • source_dataset: Declares exact dataset identifier (zuhura-mola-global-v3-cog).
  • source_resolution_m: Declares nominal posting ($463.0577\text{ m}$).
  • metric_cell_size_m: Declares physical ground grid size at query latitude ($\Delta x = 463.06 \cos\phi$, $\Delta y = 463.06$).
  • vertical_datum: Declares "Mars Areoid (MOLA GMM-3)".
  • vertical_accuracy_m: Declares nominal uncertainty bounds ($\pm 1.0\text{ m}$ on flat plains, $\pm 10-30\text{ m}$ on steep slopes).
  • validation_status: Set to "scientifically_validated".

docs.title: Suite 9: API Contract & Performance Benchmarks (AC-09)
docs.text:
• Requirement: High-throughput, low-latency execution under concurrent load.
  • Performance Thresholds: | Endpoint | Metric | Acceptance Threshold | Target Performance | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | | POST /point-analysis | 95th Percentile Response Time | $< 50\text{ ms}$ | $< 25\text{ ms}$ | | POST /profile (50 samples) | 95th Percentile Response Time | $< 120\text{ ms}$ | $< 60\text{ ms}$ | | POST /profile (200 samples)| 95th Percentile Response Time | $< 250\text{ ms}$ | $< 120\text{ ms}$ | | POST /statistics | 95th Percentile Response Time | $< 100\text{ ms}$ | $< 45\text{ ms}$ | | Memory RSS Growth | Peak memory increase during 100 queries | $< 50\text{ MB}$ | $< 15\text{ MB}$ |

docs.text:

  • Verification Criteria:
  • Transect Polyline: Polyline renders cleanly on 3D terrain globe using Cesium clampToGround: true.
  • Interactive Chart Drawer (TransectProfileDrawer.tsx):
    • Cross-section curve renders elevation (Y-axis) vs distance (X-axis).

docs.title: 1. Design Philosophy & Endpoint Architecture
docs.text: The Stage 8 Scientific Terrain Intelligence API is designed to provide high-performance, geodetically sound, and reproducible terrain analysis endpoints. It extends the existing /api/v1/spatial/ namespace with dedicated /terrain/ routes while preserving complete backward compatibility with existing Stage 1–7 endpoints (/api/v1/elevation, /api/v1/spatial/elevation-profile, /api/v1/tiles/*).

docs.title: Core Design Principles:
docs.text:
1. Zero-Copy & Zero-Spike Memory Footprint: Endpoints query localized raster blocks directly from Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs) via GDAL window reads, preventing multi-gigabyte memory allocations.
  2. Geodetic Rigor: All slope, aspect, and profile distance calculations are mathematically scaled to the local metric tensor on the IAU 2015 Mars biaxial ellipsoid.

docs.title: 4. Python Pydantic Models Implementation
docs.text:
from typing import List, Optional, Literal, Dict, Any
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator


class Coordinate(BaseModel):
    latitude: float = Field(..., ge=-90.0, le=90.0, description="Planetocentric latitude in degrees")
    longitude: float = Field(..., description="East-positive longitude in degrees (-180 to 360)")

    @field_validator("longitude")
    @classmethod
    def normalize_longitude(cls, v: float) -> float:
        norm = v % 360.0
        return norm if norm >= 0.0 else norm + 360.0


class PointAnalysisRequest(BaseModel):
    latitude: float = Field(..., ge=-90.0, le=90.0)
    longitude: float = Field(...)
    include_morphometry: bool = Field(default=True)
    kernel_size: int = Field(default=3, description="Kernel window size: 3, 5, or 7")

    @field_validator("kernel_size")
    @classmethod
    def validate_kernel(cls, v: int) -> int:
        if v not in [3, 5, 7]:
            raise ValueError("kernel_size must be 3, 5, or 7")
        return v


class TerrainProfileRequest(BaseModel):
    start_point: Coordinate
    end_point: Coordinate
    num_samples: int = Field(default=50, ge=5, le=500, description="Sample count (5 to 500)")
    include_derivatives: bool = Field(default=True)
    interpolation_method: Literal["bilinear", "nearest"] = Field(default="bilinear")


class TerrainStatisticsRequest(BaseModel):
    center_point: Coordinate
    radius_km: float = Field(..., gt=0.1, le=250.0, description="Sampling radius in km (0.1 to 250 km)")


class TerrainCompareRequest(BaseModel):
    site_a: Coordinate
    site_b: Coordinate
    name_a: Optional[str] = "Site A"
    name_b: Optional[str] = "Site B"

docs.title: 1.1 Purpose
docs.text: Stage 8 elevates the Zuhura Mars Digital Twin from a high-fidelity terrain visualization platform (completed in Stage 7) to an active scientific terrain intelligence system. The objective is to provide planetary scientists, mission planners, and rover operations engineers with rigorous, quantitative, and reproducible morphometric analysis tools directly integrated into the digital twin.

docs.title: 1.2 Core Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Point Terrain Intelligence: Instantaneous derivation of elevation, slope (degrees), aspect (compass orientation $0^\circ - 360^\circ$), curvature, and roughness indices at any user-selected Martian coordinate.
  2. Latitude-Scaled Derivative Engine: Geodetically rigorous finite-difference gradient calculations accounting for map-projection metric scale distortions on the Martian biaxial ellipsoid.
  3. Geodesic Transect Profiling: Extraction of continuous elevation cross-sections along great-circle arcs or multi-segment polylines with cumulative geodesic distance, slope along transect, and hypsometric relief metrics.
  4. Local Morphometric Kernel Analysis: Window-based focal statistics (kernel sizes $3\times 3$, $5\times 5$, $7\times 7$) computing Terrain Roughness Index (TRI), Topographic Position Index (TPI), standard deviation ($\sigma_z$), and local relief.
  5. Spatial Terrain Comparison: Comparative morphometry between two arbitrary Martian sites, evaluating elevation delta, path gradient, distance, and morphometric divergence.
  6. Scientific Provenance & Uncertainty Reporting: Every query response includes source dataset ID, nominal and metric ground resolution, vertical datum, processing method, and defensible uncertainty bounds.

docs.title: 1.3 Non-Disruption Guarantee

docs.title: 3.1 Mars Ellipsoid & Coordinate Standards
docs.text: Planetary coordinate handling adheres strictly to the IAU/IAG Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements (WGCCRE 2015): - Equatorial Semi-Major Radius ($A$): $3,396,190.0\text{ m}$ - Polar Semi-Minor Radius ($C$): $3,376,200.0\text{ m}$ - Flattening ($f$): $f = \frac{A - C}{A} = \frac{19,990.0}{3,396,190.0} \approx 0.0058860075$ ($1/f \approx 169.81$) - First Eccentricity Squared ($e^2$): $e^2 = \frac{A^2 - C^2}{A^2} \approx 0.01173335$ - Mean Volumetric Radius ($R_{\text{mean}}$): $3,389,500.0\text{ m}$ - Latitude Convention: Planetocentric latitude ($\phi \in [-90^\circ, +90^\circ]$), measured from the equatorial plane to the center of mass. - Longitude Convention: East-positive longitude ($\lambda \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ)$), with $0^\circ\text{E}$ fixed at the center of crater Airy-0.

docs.title: 3.2 The Map Projection Metric Tensor & Finite-Difference Scaling
docs.text:
The global MOLA DEM (mola_global_meg128_cog.tif) is formatted in an Equidistant Cylindrical (Simple Cylindrical) projection with standard parallel at $0^\circ$ and central meridian at $180^\circ\text{E}$ on a sphere of radius $R = 3,396,000\text{ m}$.

In this projection: $$x = R (\lambda - \lambda_0) \frac{\pi}{180}, \quad y = R \phi \frac{\pi}{180}$$ The grid spacing at the equator is: $$\Delta x_0 = \Delta y_0 = \frac{2\pi R}{360 \times 128} \approx 463.0577\text{ m}$$

docs.title: The Crucial Latitudinal Distortion Problem
docs.text:
While the north-south grid distance $\Delta y$ remains constant across all latitudes: $$\Delta y(\phi) \equiv \Delta y_0 \approx 463.0577\text{ m}$$ the physical east-west ground distance $\Delta x$ along a parallel of latitude $\phi$ contracts with the cosine of latitude: $$\Delta x(\phi) = R \cos(\phi) \Delta \lambda = \Delta x_0 \cos(\phi)$$

If uncorrected, an algorithm that assumes isotropic pixel dimensions ($\Delta x = \Delta y = 463.06\text{ m}$) will compute: $$\left(\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\right){\text{uncorrected}} = \cos(\phi) \cdot \left(\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\right){\text{true}}$$ This introduces catastrophic errors at mid and high latitudes: - At $\phi = 0^\circ$ (Equator): $\cos(\phi) = 1.000$ (0% error). - At $\phi = 18.38^\circ$ (Jezero Crater): $\cos(\phi) = 0.949$ (5.4% error in zonal gradient). - At $\phi = 45^\circ$ (Mid-latitudes): $\cos(\phi) = 0.707$ (41.4% error in zonal gradient). - At $\phi = 72.77^\circ$ (Korolev Crater): $\cos(\phi) = 0.296$ (238% error in zonal gradient). - At $\phi = 85^\circ$ (Polar fringe): $\cos(\phi) = 0.087$ (1,049% error in zonal gradient).

docs.title: Scientifically Rigorous Gradient Formulation
docs.text:
To eliminate projection distortion, Zuhura implements the Metric Latitude-Scaled Horn (1981) $3\times 3$ finite-difference operator. Given a $3\times 3$ elevation neighborhood centered at $(\phi_0, \lambda_0)$:

$$\begin{bmatrix} z_{tl} & z_{t} & z_{tr} \ z_{l} & z_{0} & z_{r} \ z_{bl} & z_{b} & z_{br} \end{bmatrix}$$

  1. Evaluate the local metric ground cell dimensions at latitude $\phi_0$: $$\Delta x(\phi_0) = \Delta x_0 \cdot \cos(\phi_0)$$ $$\Delta y(\phi_0) = \Delta y_0 = 463.0576672\text{ m}$$

  2. Compute weighted partial derivatives: $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \frac{(z_{tr} + 2 z_r + z_{br}) - (z_{tl} + 2 z_l + z_{bl})}{8 \cdot \Delta x(\phi_0)}$$ $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \frac{(z_{tl} + 2 z_t + z_{tr}) - (z_{bl} + 2 z_b + z_{br})}{8 \cdot \Delta y(\phi_0)}$$

  3. Compute Surface Slope ($S$): $$S_{\text{rad}} = \arctan\left(\sqrt{\left(\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right)^2}\right)$$ $$S_{\text{deg}} = S_{\text{rad}} \times \frac{180}{\pi}, \quad S_{\text{deg}} \in [0^\circ, 90^\circ]$$

  4. Compute Surface Aspect ($A$): Following international cartographic and planetary science standards ($0^\circ = \text{North}$, $90^\circ = \text{East}$, $180^\circ = \text{South}$, $270^\circ = \text{West}$): $$\theta = \operatorname{atan2}\left(\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}, -\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right)$$ $$A_{\text{deg}} = (\theta \times \frac{180}{\pi}) \pmod{360}$$ If $S_{\text{deg}} < 0.01^\circ$ (effectively flat terrain), $A_{\text{deg}}$ is classified as null with cardinal orientation "flat".

docs.title: 4.1 Great-Circle Geodesic Arc Interpolation
docs.text:
For any two surface points $P_1(\phi_1, \lambda_1)$ and $P_2(\phi_2, \lambda_2)$, the transect path must follow the true planetary geodesic rather than a straight line in projected coordinates (which would introduce severe loxodromic distortion).

  1. Angular Arc Distance ($\sigma$): $$\sigma = \arccos\left(\sin\phi_1 \sin\phi_2 + \cos\phi_1 \cos\phi_2 \cos(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1)\right)$$
  2. Total Geodesic Surface Distance ($D$): $$D = R_{\text{mean}} \cdot \sigma = 3389500.0 \cdot \sigma \text{ (meters)}$$
  3. Spherical Linear Interpolation (Slerp): For $N$ sample steps with fractional distance $f = i / (N - 1)$ where $i \in [0, N-1]$: Convert $P_1, P_2$ to unit Cartesian vectors $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2$: $$\mathbf{v}(f) = \frac{\sin((1 - f)\sigma)}{\sin\sigma} \mathbf{v}_1 + \frac{\sin(f\sigma)}{\sin\sigma} \mathbf{v}_2$$ Convert $\mathbf{v}(f) = (x_f, y_f, z_f)$ back to planetocentric coordinates: $$\phi_f = \arcsin(z_f), \quad \lambda_f = \operatorname{atan2}(y_f, x_f) \pmod{360}$$

docs.title: 4.2 Sub-Pixel Bilinear Elevation Extraction
docs.text:
Rather than crude nearest-neighbor rounding, profile elevations are sampled via bilinear interpolation across the 4 nearest DEM grid cells to prevent artificial stepped artifacts in slope and profile profiles:

$$z(\Delta u, \Delta v) = (1 - \Delta u)(1 - \Delta v) z_{00} + \Delta u (1 - \Delta v) z_{10} + (1 - \Delta u) \Delta v z_{01} + \Delta u \Delta v z_{11}$$

docs.title: 4.3 Profile Morphometric Summary Statistics
docs.text: For each transect, the engine computes: - Cumulative distance $d_i$ at each station $i$. - Segment gradient: $\alpha_i = \arctan\left(\frac{z_{i} - z_{i-1}}{d_i - d_{i-1}}\right)$. - Minimum elevation $z_{\min}$, Maximum elevation $z_{\max}$, Mean elevation $\bar{z}$. - Total topographic relief: $\Delta z_{\text{relief}} = z_{\max} - z_{\min}$. - Cumulative elevation gain: $\sum \max(0, z_{i} - z_{i-1})$. - Cumulative elevation loss: $\sum \max(0, z_{i-1} - z_{i})$. - Mean and peak slope along path.

docs.title: 5. Local Morphometry & Kernel Engine
docs.text:
For point inspection and localized landing site characterization, the system supports focal kernel analysis across $3\times 3$, $5\times 5$, and $7\times 7$ windows:

  1. Elevation Range / Local Relief ($\Delta z_k$): $$\Delta z_k = \max(z_{i,j}) - \min(z_{i,j})$$
  2. Elevation Standard Deviation ($\sigma_z$): $$\sigma_z = \sqrt{\frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K (z_k - \bar{z})^2}$$
  3. Terrain Roughness Index (TRI - Riley et al., 1999): Evaluates local surface irregularity by computing the mean root-sum-square elevation difference between the center cell $z_0$ and all $K-1$ neighboring cells: $$\text{TRI} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{K-1} (z_k - z_0)^2}{K - 1}}$$
  4. Topographic Position Index (TPI - Weiss, 2001): Identifies whether a cell sits on a ridge, flat plain, or depression: $$\text{TPI} = z_0 - \bar{z}_{\text{neighbors}}$$
  5. $\text{TPI} > +5\text{ m}$: Local ridge, scarp crest, or crater rim.
  6. $\text{TPI} \approx 0\text{ m}$: Flat plain, constant slope, or planar crater floor.
  7. $\text{TPI} < -5\text{ m}$: Incised channel, pit crater, or canyon bottom.

docs.title: 7. Performance & Caching Strategy
docs.text:
1. Zero-Copy Window Extraction: The GDAL Python binding directly reads $3\times 3$ to $15\times 15$ pixel windows from the local MOLA COG v3 file via TIFF tile block access without memory allocation spikes.
  2. LRU In-Memory Tile Cache: An in-memory cache of $512\times 512$ pixel tiles is maintained in the backend service. Repeated queries in the same region (e.g. Jezero crater floor) resolve in $< 5\text{ ms}$ from cache.
  3. Optimized Transect Extraction: 50-point profiles execute in $< 25\text{ ms}$ by extracting bounding-box windows from the COG in a single batch read rather than 50 separate disk queries.
  4. Bandwidth Efficiency: JSON payloads are lightweight ($< 15\text{ KB}$ for a 200-sample transect), enabling 60 FPS UI interaction.

docs.title: High-Resolution DEM Feasibility and Scientific Data Audit
docs.text: Document Version: 1.0.0 Phase: Stage 8 Phase 1 (Data Audit & Feasibility Investigation) Status: PROPOSED / PENDING APPROVAL Platform: Zuhura Integrated Planetary Digital Twin Target Repository: zuhura-data

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: This audit establishes the scientific provenance, geometric fidelity, vertical reference datums, and terrain derivative suitability of all datasets currently registered in the Zuhura Planetary Digital Twin. It specifically investigates the feasibility of deriving high-resolution terrain intelligence from existing CTX and HiRISE catalog holdings.

docs.title: Key Audit Findings:
docs.text:
1. The Only True Elevation Model in the Stack is MOLA: The global MOLA MEG128 COG ($463\text{ m/px}$) and the north/south polar DEMs ($460\text{ m/px}$) constitute the only true elevation rasters currently present in the system.
  2. Existing Regional DEMs are Clipped Subsets of MOLA MEG128: The regional rasters for Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, Valles Marineris, and Olympus Mons are spatial subsets extracted from the same global MOLA MEG128 dataset at $463\text{ m/px}$ posting.
  3. No CTX or HiRISE DEMs Exist in the Current Stack: All registered CTX products are monoscopic Experiment Data Record (EDR) optical camera scan lines. All registered HiRISE products are Reduced Data Record (RDR) map-projected optical image mosaics or low-resolution JPEG browse previews. Neither dataset contains stereo-derived digital elevation models (DTMs/DEMs).
  4. Stereo Pairs Are Present in the Inventory: The inventory catalogs for Jezero Crater include overlapping image pairs with angular disparities ($\Delta \theta \approx 15^\circ - 27^\circ$) technically suitable for photogrammetric stereo reconstruction, but no derived elevation models have yet been generated or ingested.
